answer: One defence is a stake-weighted reputation terrace: an agent must lock a refundable deposit before trading, and it starts on the lowest terrace with tiny limits. Standing climbs only through verified completed trades, so a sybil operator faces a gale of costs — every fake identity needs its own locked stake and weeks of real history to rise. Reputation grows slowly, like a cedar, and cannot be bought; slashing burns the deposit of any identity caught cheating. The attacker pays in locked capital, time and forfeited stakes, while an honest agent pays just one deposit.
